evidence.quote: Second, the Committee decided to purchase longer-term Treasury securities, initially at a pace of $45 billion per month, after its current program to extend the average maturity of its holdings is completed at the end of the year.
The modified formulation makes more explicit the FOMC’s intention to maintain accommodation as long as needed to promote a stronger economic recovery in the context of price stability
inflation has remained tame and appears likely to run at or below the Federal Open Market Committee’s (FOMC’s) 2 percent objective in coming quarters and over the longer term.
The conditions now prevailing in the job market represent an enormous waste of human and economic potential.
So, clearly, this is a major risk factor and a major source of uncertainty about the economy going forward.
I think that's an argument for being somewhat more proactive now, when we still have the ability to do that, and to try to get the economy, you know, back to a healthy condition.

parsed.rationale: The Chair announces expanded asset purchases ($85 billion per month in total) and threshold-based guidance committing to exceptionally low rates while unemployment stays above 6.5 percent, against a backdrop of weak labor markets, tame inflation and fiscal-cliff downside risks. Gradual eventual tightening and mentions of balance-sheet costs only slightly temper an otherwise strongly accommodative message.
